PainterlyNPR__GlbScenes__Config__Meta.ConfigLabel: PainterlyNPR - GLB Scenes: Glass, Windows and Doors
PainterlyNPR__GlbScenes__Config__Meta.ConfigNote: How a project's own model (a GLB scene) tells its glass, window frames and doors from the rest, by tag, by material and by name, and how each pane of glass becomes a window record the shadow lines draw from.
PainterlyNPR__GlbScenes__Config__Meta.Source: Adam, 30-Oct-2026: "Naming from sketchup and using the SSOT Windows tags (there is one for existing and proposed) same with doors so use a tipple method tag/material/naming" (v0.8.16)

RecognitionNotes.Order: Glass first (its material, then its tag or name), then Window, then Door; nothing recognised keeps its object's class
RecognitionNotes.Tags: The part of a flattened node's name before '::' (TrueVision's GLB builder buckets faces as <tag>::<material>, so the SSOT tags 14__ExistingBuilding__Windows, 24__ProposedBuilding__Windows, 15__ and 25__ ... Doors arrive here), or a node's extras.tag
RecognitionNotes.Materials: The part after '::' (the SketchUp material's own name, kept even in a whitecard export) and the glTF material's name; case is ignored
RecognitionNotes.Names: The node's and the mesh's names: an instanced component arrives under its definition's name
RecognitionNotes.SeeThrough: A glTF material blended or less opaque than this is glass, whatever its name (TrueVision's builder passes the tray's Opacity through)

WindowsNotes.WeldM: Corners closer than this are one corner when a pane's triangles are joined
WindowsNotes.CoplanarDot: Triangles of one pane face the same way to within this (about 2.5 degrees)
WindowsNotes.MinSideM: A pane narrower or shorter than this is a glass edge or a sliver, not a pane
WindowsNotes.DuplicateM: Two panes facing the same way, overlapping and this close are the two faces of one sheet of glass: the outer one is kept
WindowsNotes.ProbeOffsetsM: How far beyond each upright edge of a pane the model is probed for what stands in front of the glass there
WindowsNotes.ProbeHeights: Where up each upright edge it is probed, as shares of the pane's height
WindowsNotes.MinRevealM: Less than this in front of the glass is flush: that side casts nothing
WindowsNotes.MaxRevealM: The deepest reveal looked for in front of the glass
WindowsNotes.BarStepM: The spacing of the probes across a pane that find glazing bars standing in front of one sheet of glass
WindowsNotes.BarRows: The heights, as shares of the pane, of the rows of bar probes; a bar must show in two of them
WindowsNotes.BarMaxWidthM: Anything wider in front of the glass is not a bar (a transom, a frame)
WindowsNotes.BarMinDepthM: A bar stands at least this far in front of the glass
WindowsNotes.BarMatchM: A bar found in two rows within this of each other is one bar
